_comment: F-16A Block 10/15 Level-2 geometry inputs: per-surface planform (wing / horizontal tail / vertical tail), fuselage envelope, and engine/duct geometry. These are Brandt-F16-A.xls Main-tab hardcoded inputs (VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json), NOT the T.O. 1F-16A-1-manual values (HT S=63.70 ft2, VT S=54.75 ft2) currently hand-frozen in the legacy F16GeomL2.m/F16GeomL3.m — see examples/F16A/F16GeomL2.md ('S_exposed_ht'/'S_exposed_vt' rows) for the naming-concern discussion of why those legacy literals differ from Brandt's own Main-tab values used here.
_l3_merge_note: 2026-07-22: Geometry's L3 tier was eliminated (user decision — see src/disciplines/geometry/GeomL2.md's dated note); this file is the merge of the former geometry_L2.json and geometry_L3.json. The tc_root/tc_tip splits (HT/VT) and the engine block below were previously L3-only fields; geometry_L3.json is deleted.
_source: VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/f16a_geometry.json (wing / pitch_ctrl / vert_tail / fuselage / engine blocks); src/disciplines/geometry/GeomL2.md; examples/F16A/F16GeomL2.md

wing._note_tc: Wing airfoil (NACA 1404/64A204) is treated as constant-thickness across the span in the existing F16GeomL2.m/F16GeomL3.m model — no root/tip t/c split exists for the wing (unlike HT/VT below), so a single tc_ratio is carried here rather than a tc_root/tc_tip pair.

horizontal_tail._note: Brandt's Main-tab 'pitch_ctrl' column — the all-moving stabilator.
horizontal_tail._source_tc: T.O. 1F-16A-1, Sec I — biconvex root ~6%, tip ~3.5%. Matches existing F16GeomL3.m literals tc_r_ht/tc_t_ht; kept as-is per examples/F16A/F16GeomL2.md (formerly F16GeomL3.md) (this is NOT a Brandt value — Brandt's own workbook uses one constant tc per lifting surface for its S_wet formula; the user's decision was to preserve this T.O.-derived root/tip split rather than force it to Brandt's single uniform value). Used by the Roskam Eq. 12.1 variable-tc option (GeomL2.compute_roskam_planform, formerly GeomL3); the uniform-tc Brandt option (compute_wet_planform) uses tc_ratio above instead.

vertical_tail._source_tc: T.O. 1F-16A-1, Sec I — biconvex root ~5.3%, tip ~3.0%. Matches existing F16GeomL3.m literals tc_r_vt/tc_t_vt; kept as-is per examples/F16A/F16GeomL2.md (formerly F16GeomL3.md) (NOT a Brandt value — same rationale as horizontal_tail._source_tc above).

fuselage._source: f16a_geometry.json:fuselage (Brandt-F16-A.xls Main!B32=length, C32=max width, D32=max height — exact cell locations confirmed live 2026-07-21 against Brandt-F16-A.xls, VnV/BrandtF16A/todo.md Finding 4, range Main!A31:D32)

engine._note: These four fields feed the planned nacelle-diameter/length formula D_engine=sqrt(T_AB_SLS_lb/1900), L_engine=4.5*D_engine (VnV/BrandtF16A/readme_geom.md Section 3; VnV/BrandtF16A/GroundTruth/cell-map.md 'Engn(s)' section) — a planned computed replacement for F16GeomL2.m's (formerly F16GeomL3.m's) current hand-frozen D_inlet=3.4 ft/D_exit=2.9 ft/L_duct=14.0 ft T.O. estimates. D_inlet/D_exit/L_duct are therefore intentionally NOT included here as raw inputs: once the nacelle-geometry formula is implemented they become computed quantities, not hardcoded ones. Duct S_wet itself (GeomL2.get_S_wet_duct / compute_s_wet_duct, Raymer 6th ed. §7.3) uses D_inlet/D_exit/L_duct directly, not these four fields.
